Totally agree—it doesn’t make sense that a “free plan” user can’t even reach the core app before being forced through the premium onboarding. My fix would be to let free users reach the main `MainTabView` immediately while still offering the premium upsell from Profile (and other upgrade touchpoints). Concretely, I’d:

- Gate the “must-finish paywall” logic behind actual premium intent. In `opalcloneApp.swift`, let users who haven’t completed onboarding choose a lightweight, optional intro (or skip entirely) that ends in the free experience rather than `PremiumOnboardingView`.
- Reuse or simplify the existing onboarding screens so paywall content only shows when someone explicitly taps “Upgrade” (from the profile sheet, limited free feature, etc.), not on app launch.
- Keep the premium purchase flow wired up via `PremiumManager.shared`, so the upgrade still happens through StoreKit when the user asks for it; we just stop making it mandatory to see the app.

That way the “Start Free Trial” button becomes an opt‑in upsell instead of a roadblock, and the free tier really feels accessible. Next steps (if you’d like them): 1) refactor the launch logic to drop the paywall requirement, 2) tighten the profile upgrade sheet so it uses the existing StoreKit flow, 3) add tests/manual QA to confirm free users can browse without signing up.
